details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:
`v0.5.23-rocm720-mi35x-20261118` and `-20261119` both return 404 on Docker Hub (rechecked 22:24), so the newest `rocm720-mi35x` image is from Nov 17.
Kimi-K3.1-Pro failed in both completed nightlies since Nov 18 16:07.
The kernel tests fail on rocm724 (Nov 18) and rocm720 (Nov 19), and pass on rocm10.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#51000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51000) ([`ea93e2fc`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/ea93e2fcd0d1566f4817c0fe8ddfe6d8006908fd)) added a gfx950-only `RUN` at `docker/rocm.Dockerfile:860` that builds the Rust TreeCore. `torch_build.py:15-16` accepts only torch 2.11–2.15, and the ROCm 7.2.0 image has torch 2.9.1. The same PR sets `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=never`, but CI runs from an editable checkout with no bundled TreeCore, so any rank that picks Rust crashes.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: the kernel-test part (`[MEDIUM]`, [#50998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50998) and #51000) rests on two data points, and the rocm720 aiter pin `285579b6` differs from rocm10's.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found (rechecked 22:24). [#46823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46823) and [#48112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48112) only change the toolchain probe.
On a branch, skip the TreeCore `RUN` for `*rocm720*` and build `GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm720`.
Then re-run `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-kimi-k31-pro` with `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto`.

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:
The DeepSeek-V4.1 crash and the Kimi-K3 collapse first appeared in the Nov 18 05:21 nightly and came back on Nov 19. The last pass was Nov 17.
The `--monokernel-backend` error reached the nightly on Nov 19.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#48414](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48414) ([`6321f714`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/6321f714ddd9c5da511b0cfefa0ebabc4277cf36)) made `megakernel_tensor_graph_variants()` (`binding.py:1401`) read `installed.tensor_entry`. sgl-amd-mono's DeepSeek-V4.1 `_Entries` stub has no such attribute, so draft CUDA-graph capture fails.
The same PR changed `KimiK3DecoderLayer.forward`, which may explain the Kimi-K3 collapse (KL 1.13, gsm8k 4.7%; `[MEDIUM]`).

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: the changed Kimi-K3 lines look like NVIDIA mega-MoE paths, and the same image also bumped aiter ([#50759](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50759)).

GLM-5.3: `[HIGH]` [sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono/pull/123) and [sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono/pull/126) collided when merged.
✅ [sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#158](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono/pull/158) for the flag.
✅ [sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#152](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono/pull/152) for `--mxfp4` only.
❌ none for `tensor_entry`, the Kimi-K3 collapse, or the 3 GLM-5.3 unit tests.
